firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Thank you for clarifying that an arXiv preprint is permitted ([745872](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent-paper/discussion/745872)) and that the substantially extended study described after a public pilot is a valid submission ([745150](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent-paper/discussion/745150)). Could you clarify how the unpublished requirement applies to this narrower, non-arXiv case?

I have a private teaching Notebook that formats older aggregate results from matched unpatched/reference CPU verifier controls on four public development tasks, later separate verifier checks, and a post-run source adjudication. Those later checks produced additional verifier and source-review evidence; the Notebook only presents the saved aggregates and makes no new Agent calls or method-effectiveness comparison. It explains test collection, dependency identity and target assertions, and distinguishes verifier outcomes from normal Agent completion. Its small formatting code and prose disclose no Agent strategy, prompts, weights, task-specific patch/test/trajectory text, raw competition data or submission archive.

A later Paper would audit eight public-development Agent task cases and a separate same-task verifier control. Two task identities occur in both the older CPU controls and the later Agent cases, and part of the evaluation framing overlaps. The proposed teaching Notebook does not contain the later Agent case results or that separate control. If the Notebook were published before the deadline and cited as prior engineering teaching material, would that prevent the later case-audit Paper from meeting “original, unpublished research”? Would the new case evidence and analysis be assessed as the Paper’s contribution while the earlier tutorial is treated as prior disclosure?

Separately, would the answer differ for a non-arXiv Notebook that publishes the same case-study results later used in the Paper, without substantial additional evidence or analysis? The Submission Requirements allow a public Notebook as a project link, but I do not assume that this also decides earlier standalone publication.
